title: Praise God the Lord, Ye Sons of Men
description: Praise God the Lord, Ye Sons of Men in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Nikolaus Herman wrote these words in German. August Crull's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 157.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Praise God the Lord, ye sons of men, Be-fore His high-est throne, To day He o-pens heaven a-gain And gives us His own Son.

lines: Praise God the Lord, ye sons of men,
Before His highest throne,
To-day He opens heaven again
And gives us His own Son.
He leaves His heavenly Father’s throne,
Is born an infant small,
And in a manger, poor and lone,
Lies in a humble stall.
He lays aside His power divine,
A servant’s form doth take;
In want and lowness He doth pine
Who heaven and earth did make.
He nestles at His mother’s breast,
Her milk His food must be;
Whom saints and angels call the Blest,
Of David’s house is He.
’Tis He who in these latter days
From Judah’s tribe should come,
By whom the Lord again would raise
His Church, His Christendom.
A wondrous change which He doth make!
He takes our flesh and blood
And lays aside for sinners’ sake
His majesty of God.
He serves that I a lord may be;
A great exchange, indeed!
Could Jesus’ love do more for me
To help me in my need?
He opens us again the door
Of Paradise to-day;
The cherub guards the gate no more.
To God our thanks we pay.

licence: Public domain: Nikolaus Herman died in 1561; August Crull died in 1923.
credits: Words by Nikolaus Herman (died 1561), translated by August Crull (1845–1923), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
